title: He sold a company he built from scratch for over nine billion dollars - the largest software deal of its time.
sources: CNBC, Dec 8, 2023 - How a 75-year-old Indian-American tech entrepreneur is betting $1 billion of his own fortune on AI's future
caption:
He sold a company he built from scratch for over nine billion dollars - the largest software deal of its time.

Born in Karachi, his family moved to India after Partition. He studied at IIT Bombay before earning a PhD from Carnegie Mellon, then moved to the US to build his career in enterprise software.

Wadhwani founded Aspect Development in Silicon Valley in 1991. Eight years later, i2 Technologies acquired it for $9.3 billion in stock - at the time, the Wall Street Journal called it the largest software deal ever made.

Wadhwani went on to found Symphony Technology Group and Symphony AI and now runs the Wadhwani Foundation, funding economic development back in India. One engineering degree, three decades and a company sold for nine billion dollars - proof of what an IIT education abroad can turn into.
